q1: SELECT A.PROJECT_ID, ROUND(AVG(B.EXPERIENCE_YEARS), 2) AS AVERAGE_YEARS FROM PROJECT AS A INNER JOIN EMPLOYEE AS B ON A.EMPLOYEE_ID = B.EMPLOYEE_ID GROUP BY A.PROJECT_ID
q2: SELECT DISTINCT P.PROJECT_ID, ROUND(AVG(EXPERIENCE_YEARS),2)AVERAGE_YEARS FROM PROJECT P JOIN EMPLOYEE E ON P.EMPLOYEE_ID = E.EMPLOYEE_ID GROUP BY P.PROJECT_ID
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT A.PROJECT_ID, ROUND(AVG(B.EXPERIENCE_YEARS), 2) AS AVERAGE_YEARS FROM PROJECT AS A INNER JOIN EMPLOYEE AS B ON A.EMPLOYEE_ID = B.EMPLOYEE_ID GROUP BY A.PROJECT_ID
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT DISTINCT P.PROJECT_ID, ROUND(AVG(EXPERIENCE_YEARS),2)AVERAGE_YEARS FROM PROJECT P JOIN EMPLOYEE E ON P.EMPLOYEE_ID = E.EMPLOYEE_ID GROUP BY P.PROJECT_ID
explanation: Both queries aim to calculate the average years of experience for employees associated with each project. The difference in syntax (INNER JOIN vs JOIN, DISTINCT in Q2) does not affect the outcome as long as the data does not contain duplicates in the PROJECT table that would be filtered out by DISTINCT in Q2.
